reason: The original kernels, adapted from vLLM, had the barriers 'due to bug in Triton compiler'. reason: The maintainer gave four reasons: the fused qk norm had no fallback, which broke the AMD diffusion CI; the fused path should be chosen by can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm; a .contiguous() on non-contiguous q and k is a costly copy; and the benchmark had no warmup. The author answered that apply_qk_norm already checks can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm and has a fallback, and that the change had passed CI. It did not come back; the maintainer planned a refactor of the qk-norm logic.

reason: With auto, FlashInfer's mm_fp4 picks the cuDNN FP4 GEMM when cuDNN is 9.15 or newer and CUDA is 13, and that backend was slower, also with cuDNN 9.18 (FlashInfer issue #2375). The author rolled back to the CUTLASS backend 12 days after the merge. No reland was found.

title: optimize get_topk_ragged by fusing get k and k_scale triton kernel
found_by: a user on AMD with a long context, and the maintainer, five days after the merge
stated: after this PR was merged, DeepSeek-v3.2 encounters the following error when running with a long context (> 65,536 tokens): Triton Error [HIP]: Code: 1, Messsage: invalid argument. This occurs because the Triton kernel grid is configured as grid = (seq_num, max_seq_len).
reason: The fused kernel launches grid = (seq_num, max_seq_len). The y dimension of a launch grid is limited to 65,535, so the launch fails for contexts of more than 65,535 tokens; a user hit it on AMD ('invalid argument'), and the maintainer also found errors with very long contexts. It was reverted five days after the merge and did not come back. warpDRF finds this launch-limit violation at the call site (run of 2026-10-13), but its reviewer filter drops grid limits.

title: [diffusion]: Improve layerwise offload buffer reuse and shared-storage handling
found_by: the maintainer, the next day
stated: While the original PR reported decreased 'Peak GPU memory' metrics, this reduction is misleading as it only reflects PyTorch's allocated memory tracking, not actual VRAM consumption.
reason: The pool keeps up to 2 x prefetch_size buffers per tensor size on the GPU. torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() went down, but torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved(), the physical VRAM that the process holds, went up. Thus the reported gain was a measurement artifact. The author agreed after a new test: the peak VRAM stays the same, and only the allocated memory decreases.

reason: The revert (#29452) gives no reason. The reland #29463 says that the PR dropped the gsm8k score of test_moe_ep_extra.py from about 0.7 to 0.005, and explains why. Inside the routed call, dispose_tensor() calls .set_(torch.empty(0)) on the original hidden_states, so the shared-expert GEMM that launched next captured data_ptr() == 0 into the decode CUDA graph, and at each replay it read from a null address. The reland keeps the new stream assignment and launches the shared expert first; 'source-order alone is sufficient'.

The router GEMM came back in #35121 as a bf16 GEMM with fp32 accumulation and output, with fp32 compute kept for NemotronH.

title: [torch.compile] Improve Cold Start for MoEs
found_by: the author (planned)

reason: A planned replacement, not a failure. The workaround assumed that the custom MoE ops always run in order. It gave garbled output for ERNIE-4.5-VL (two experts, one of them used in decode), fixed by turning it off for that model (#35587), and it was turned off with speculative decoding (#33624). With torch 2.11, #35475 lifts the layer names as graph inputs (register_opaque_type with hoist=True) and drops the workaround; #38123 later allows strings in custom ops without slower compilation.

reason: A single-commit bisect showed that DeepSeek-V4 Flash with DP 4 and EP answered 'the the the the …' in place of 'Paris'. The revert does not state the mechanism. The removed code comment calls the moved ops 'metadata-dependent', and a later revert (#52836) says that the same narrow eager region corrupted output on Model Runner V1 (#52401 restored the wide region there). title: [KV Offload] Use background thread for mmap / cpu_tensors pinning
found_by: a user report (#46933), four days after the merge
stated: I believe there is a race between _pin_cpu_tensors and CUDA graph captures.
reason: With CPU KV offloading, CUDA graph capture hung (issue #46933). The background thread called cudaHostRegister while the main thread captured CUDA graphs, and the call returned cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported ('The operation is not permitted when the stream is capturing'). Joining the thread before the capture fixed it; the maintainers preferred the revert, five days after the merge. A pinning that waits on events per block was proposed as the proper solution.

title: [Kernel] Add weightless RMSNorm CUDA kernels for has_weight=False (#41430)
found_by: the XPU maintainers, 12 days after the merge
stated: On XPU, weightless RMSNorm (weight=None) ... falls back to the native eager implementation, which decomposes into many small aten ops (pow, mean, rsqrt, mul, add). At small batch sizes ... this fallback significantly increases the number of CPU-dispatched kernels and hurts TPOT.
reason: On XPU, with weight=None the layer fell back to the native eager implementation, which splits into many small aten ops; at small batch sizes the model is bound by host dispatch, so TPOT got worse. The XPU part was reverted 12 days after the merge; the XPU kernels support weightless RMSNorm since (vllm-xpu-kernels #441).

title: [Sampler] Stop upcasting logits to fp32 in apply_sampling_params
found_by: the nightly CI (an automatic revert), three days after

reason: The CI failure analyzer linked the PR to one nightly failure: the MTP variant of Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4 hung in sample_tokens with DP 2, while the non-MTP variant passed. Its explanation, that the in-place bf16 change 'plausibly corrupts spec-decode verification numerics and desyncs the DP=2 ranks', is a guess, and a maintainer at first doubted that the PR was the cause. It did not come back.

title: [Perf][GLM-5.2] Blackwell decode optimizations

reason: No failure. The PR merged without the proper review, and the reviewer objected to some design choices. It came back as focused PRs (#49791, #49792, #49793, #50230).

title: [Perf][ROCm] Dual-stream decode with hipgraphs
found_by: AMD CI (gsm8k, Qwen3.5 with DP 2 and EP), the same day
stated: Qwen3.5 uses the same tensor for hidden state and shared expert inputs, and never creates any copies of either tensor throughout the MoE. This causes a race condition during multi-stream. Specifically, it uses the same tensors because it's not quantizing the routed experts' input.
reason: The AMD CI gsm8k test failed for Qwen3.5 with DP 2 and EP. The reland explains: when the routed experts are not quantized, the shared-expert input on the auxiliary stream is the same tensor as the hidden state of the routed path on the main stream, with no copy, so the two streams race; quantized routed experts copy their input first, so they do not alias. The reland turns the overlap off on ROCm when the routed input is not quantized, and it merged 17 days later. The texts do not name the kernel that writes the shared tensor.

title: [DSv4 Perf] Adaptive topk width, 1.0% E2E throughput improvement
found_by: users under concurrent load (#52448, #48089), 19 days after the merge
stated: The C128A metadata builder runs before FULL CUDA graph replay, but the sparse decode consumer is captured and reuses its capture-time row layout. ... Row 0 still started at offset 0, but later rows could be read from stale offsets.
reason: Under concurrent requests at long contexts, DeepSeek-V4 output was corrupted (#52448; unbalanced reasoning tags, #48089). The metadata builder runs outside the CUDA graph and wrote rows with a stride that depends on the batch, while the captured consumer kept the stride from capture time, so the rows after the first were read at stale offsets. It was reverted 19 days after the merge, and it came back in #52823, which keeps capacity-strided slices, asserts that the strides match, and adds a CUDA graph test.

title: [DSv4 Perf] Optimize workspace reuse for eager break
found_by: the maintainers, 19 days after the merge
stated: The model-wide scratch pool can reuse storage across layers and CUDA streams without the caching allocator's stream/event lifetime tracking. That allows a producer to overwrite shared workspace while a previous consumer may still be using it.
reason: The pool gave the same storage to different layers and CUDA streams, but nothing recorded which stream still used a buffer, which the caching allocator does with stream and event lifetimes. Thus a producer could overwrite a workspace that an earlier consumer on another stream still read. The revert, 19 days after the merge, restored allocator-backed temporary buffers 'until safe cross-stream synchronization is implemented'. It also notes that the narrow eager region corrupted Model Runner V1 output (#52401). It did not come back.

title: [Kernel] Gemma-4 FA4 FP8 Kernel
found_by: the nightly performance test (H200), five days after
stated: This regresses Gemma4 on Hopper nightly ... compared to using Triton
reason: The nightly H200 performance test showed a regression for Gemma-4 31B FP8. The author found the cause: the FA4 FP8-KV kernel does not support the bidirectional attention of the multimodal prefix, but the backend selection chose it also when 'use_bidirectional_attention' is 'vision' with --language-only, so Gemma-4 emitted special tokens, which the benchmark counted as slow output. The resubmit #53175 fixes the backend selection, and it merged a month later.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Tune FlashInfer experts to scheduler token limit

title: [warmup] overlap renderer warmup and engine core initialization
found_by: post-merge CI (H200 and MI300), the same day
stated: a live Python background thread is doing multimodal processor work while engine-core initialization forks.
reason: Main CI hung at start-up in the multimodal Whisper jobs on H200 and MI300 until their timeouts (75 and 25 minutes). The captured stack shows the warmup thread inside Whisper spectrogram preprocessing while the main thread forked the engine-core processes; a fork while another thread holds locks can deadlock the child. A maintainer noted that the same CI step had passed on the PR. A new version merged a week later (#54557).

title: [6/N][warmup][DSv4] Migrate sampling, and DFlash JIT kernels
found_by: post-merge CI (H200 time limits), the same day
reason: The revert (#56654) gives no reason. #56649 shows the effect: with the explicit warmups, H200 CI lanes exceeded their time budgets (for example 32 JIT warmups that took 415.65 s in one job), and after the revert the affected lanes passed within their original budgets. #58092 later registered the MRV2 sampler JIT warmups again for ROCm. Issues also report CPU Triton fallbacks that the PR left unused (#58214, #55005).

title: [ROCm][Perf] Add bpreshuffled blockscaled fp8 GEMM
found_by: AMD engineers, the day after the merge
stated: When testing gsm8k for DeepSeek-V4 on AMD GPUs using latest vLLM main, the acc value becomes 0
reason: The next day, a ROCm engineer saw garbage output with DeepSeek-V3 TP8 and a failed start with DeepSeek-V4 TP8. The fix #56433 found four problems in the new kernel's use, for example that it read the activation scale as column-major while the callers emit row-major scales, and that models such as DeepSeek-V4 shuffle some weights again after the kernel B-preshuffles them. DeepSeek-V4 gsm8k still fell to 0, so #57132 reverted both PRs six days after the merge.
